opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but admin is only for the owning role (Engineer). As a full-time employee, max is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Traci Lowe (E041) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write requires advanced training; never admin). Requested admin on Source Code, so grant max read.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requested admin access to Source Code. Both notes agree her role is Analyst, and Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted regardless (never admin for non-owning role/contractor). There is a conflict: HR lists her as full_time (max write), while the Security database lists her as a contractor with basic security training (max read, since write requires advanced training). Relying on the Security record for the security-relevant attributes (contractor + basic training), the maximum allowed level is read. The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum: read.
